note: Companies the long-term investing paper account may buy. Descriptions are a starting point from general knowledge (2026-11-16); the weekly research run checks and updates them, adds or removes companies, and records the date and sources it used. The trading rules only use prices; this list decides WHICH companies are eligible.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.what: Designs the graphics processors (GPUs) and networking used to train and run most AI models.
companies.potential: AI data-centre spending is still growing fast: quarterly revenue (to 25 Oct 2026) was 115.8 billion USD, more than double a year earlier, with about 130 billion USD expected next quarter.
companies.risks: Founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned on 12 Nov 2026; the CFO is interim CEO and the stock fell about 10% after. Also very high expectations, customers building their own chips, and export limits (no China data-centre sales assumed).

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.what: Windows, Office, the Azure cloud and a large stake in OpenAI's technology.
companies.potential: Azure cloud grew 48% in Jul-Sep 2026; companies keep buying AI capacity.
companies.risks: Huge AI data-centre costs (about 45 billion USD in one quarter); competition in cloud.

companies.name: Alphabet (Google)
companies.what: Google search and ads, YouTube, Google Cloud, its own AI models (Gemini) and AI chips (TPUs); also quantum computing research.
companies.potential: Google Cloud revenue roughly doubled (+103%) in Jul-Sep 2026; quantum and self-driving (Waymo) as long-term options.
companies.risks: Spending on AI is now larger than the cash it brings in (negative free cash flow, much more debt); AI chatbots changing search habits; regulation. The stock had its worst one-day drop on record in early Nov 2026.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.what: Online shop and AWS, the largest cloud provider; builds its own AI chips.
companies.potential: AWS grew 39% in Jul-Sep 2026 with a very large order backlog.
companies.risks: Spending about 220 billion USD on data centres in 2026, so more money goes out than comes in; thin shop margins.

companies.name: Meta Platforms
companies.what: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp; earns from ads; large AI research and open AI models.
companies.potential: Better ad targeting with AI; AI assistants.
companies.risks: Very large AI spending (135-145 billion USD in 2026) paid partly with debt; spending on virtual reality; regulation.

companies.name: Apple
companies.what: iPhone, Mac and services like the App Store.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.what: Networking chips and custom AI chips for large cloud companies, plus infrastructure software.
companies.potential: Custom AI chips for Google, Meta and others.
companies.risks: Depends on a few big customers.

companies.name: AMD
companies.what: Processors for PCs and servers and AI accelerators competing with NVIDIA.
companies.potential: Winning a share of AI accelerator spending.

companies.name: TSMC
companies.what: Taiwanese company that manufactures most of the world's advanced chips, including NVIDIA's and Apple's.
companies.potential: Record sales: October 2026 revenue up about 60% on a year earlier.

companies.name: Micron Technology
companies.what: US maker of memory chips, including the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) that sits next to NVIDIA's and AMD's AI chips.
companies.potential: AI chips need lots of memory: revenue in Jun-Aug 2026 was 54.2 billion USD, almost 5 times a year earlier, and most of its 2027 HBM supply is already agreed with customers.
companies.risks: Memory has always gone from boom to bust; SK hynix and Samsung are bigger in HBM and adding capacity; depends on AI spending staying high.

companies.name: ASML
companies.what: Dutch maker of the lithography machines needed to make advanced chips; near-monopoly in the most advanced machines.

companies.name: Palantir
companies.what: Data and AI software for governments and companies.
companies.potential: Revenue grew 96% in Jul-Sep 2026 and the company raised its 2026 forecast to about 8.5 billion USD.
companies.risks: Very high valuation; falls hard when the whole AI sector sells off, even after good results.

companies.name: CrowdStrike
companies.potential: Security needs grow with cloud and AI.

companies.name: IonQ
companies.what: Builds quantum computers using trapped ions, sold through the cloud.
companies.potential: Largest of the quantum companies by revenue: 2026 forecast raised to 505-515 million USD (partly from buying other companies).
companies.risks: Still loses money; sold 2 billion USD of new shares and paid for acquisitions in shares, so each share owns less; stock fell about a third in a month.

companies.name: Rigetti Computing
companies.what: Builds superconducting quantum chips and computers.
companies.risks: Revenue only 1.4 million USD in Jul-Sep 2026 (below forecasts); its CEO said quantum computers can't yet beat normal computers on cost, maybe in about three years. Losses; extreme price swings.

companies.name: D-Wave Quantum
companies.what: Quantum annealing computers for optimisation problems, sold as a cloud service.
companies.risks: Tiny revenue (4.5 million USD in Jul-Sep 2026) and new orders fell; losses; stock down about two thirds this year.

companies.name: Invesco QQQ (Nasdaq-100 fund)
companies.what: A fund that holds the 100 largest non-financial Nasdaq companies.
companies.potential: Broad big-tech exposure in one purchase.
companies.risks: Falls with the whole tech market.

companies.name: VanEck Semiconductor fund
companies.what: A fund holding the largest chip companies.
companies.risks: Chip stocks swing a lot: the chip index fell about 38% from its June 2026 peak by early November.
